note: Researched supplier sets for the Compare tab, one per speciality. HUMAN-CURATED — no automation writes this file. Until 05/08/2026 these lived hard-coded inside app/comptab.js, which meant adding a speciality was a code change to a file that also holds the tab's rendering; there were two, and eleven specialities carried notices. Moving them here makes growth a data edit that verify.py can gate. app/comptab.js still holds vascular and continence as a baked fallback so the tab is never empty if this file cannot be fetched; anything here overrides it.
sourceRule: Every framework name, its dates and its supplier list come from that framework's own contract launch brief on supplychain.nhs.uk, fetched directly. Brand names come from the NHS Supply Chain online catalogue entry for the supplier's own NPC codes — the procurement record, not the supplier's marketing. Nothing here is inferred from a trade summary or a comparison table.

bloodcoll.label: Blood collection / phlebotomy

route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Blood Collection Devices (1 lot, 19 suppliers, 9 of them new)

bloodcoll.routeNote: One lot covering the whole category. It replaced and combined the former Blood Collection Systems and Blood Lancets framework and the Blood Culture Collection Systems framework, so a trust's incumbent may sit on it under a different arrangement than the one they remember. Blood collection is nested under Vascular access in the Hub's speciality list because the same accounts touch both — but the buyer is usually pathology or phlebotomy, not the vascular access team. More companies from the Hub's verified supplier index are listed below without catalogue-level product detail yet (marked as such in their row) — added 02/09/2026 from the index the Hub already held, not fresh research.

suppliers.brands: BD Vacutainer
suppliers.note: Incumbent across most of the category. KFK036, its multi-sampling adaptor, is on Protect Demand Management — see live issues.

suppliers.brands: Vacuette
suppliers.note: KFK232 Luer multisampling adaptor and the Vacuette Quickshield safety tube holder (450230). Named in ICN 3385 as an alternative to BD's KFK036.

suppliers.brands: S-Monovette
suppliers.note: Not a like-for-like swap: Sarstedt's own page describes S-Monovette drawing by aspiration ("the plunger rod is gently pulled") as well as by vacuum, so moving to it changes technique and training, not just a code. Holds four of the seven codes in the adaptor section (KCM096, KCM114, KCM128, FNG85313).

suppliers.brands: SOL-M · SOL-CARE
suppliers.note: FNG85289 multi-sampling Luer adaptor holder, named in ICN 3385 as an alternative; also the SOL-CARE single-use safety tube holder (BCA019).

suppliers.brands: Prosum
suppliers.note: KFK978 sampling Luer adaptor, named in ICN 3385 as an alternative, plus the Prosum sterile sampling cap holder (BCH002).

suppliers.brands: Unistik
suppliers.note: Awarded on the framework; lancets and capillary sampling rather than venous tubes.

suppliers.brands: Nipro
suppliers.note: One of the nine suppliers new to this framework at the 2025 award.

suppliers.brands: Vygon
suppliers.note: Awarded on the framework; also on both vascular access frameworks, so often already a known name in the account.

cardiology.routeNote: Nine lots: ultrasound gels, adult ECG electrodes, paediatric/neonatal ECG electrodes, neurology electrodes and needles, pre-wired electrodes, foetal scalp electrodes, abdominal CTG belts, defibrillation electrodes and pads, and related consumables. Defibrillation pads are Lot 8. The set below is the defibrillation and ECG electrode players, not all 37 awarded suppliers. skin-prep.label: Skin prep and antisepsis

route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Skin Cleansing, Disinfection and Hygiene (6 lots, 29 suppliers). Lot 5 is Skin Disinfectant (Medicinal Products), Lot 6 is Pre-operative Skin Preparation

skin-prep.routeNote: Six lots: patient cleansing wipes, waterless bathing, personal care, antimicrobial cleansing, skin disinfectant (medicinal products) and pre-operative skin preparation. The set below is the skin-antisepsis players, not all 29 awarded suppliers. Note that a 2% chlorhexidine / 70% alcohol applicator is a licensed medicinal product, so it sits in Lot 5 rather than with the wipes. More companies from the Hub's verified supplier index are listed below without catalogue-level product detail yet (marked as such in their row) — added 02/09/2026 from the index the Hub already held, not fresh research.

suppliers.brands: ChloraPrep · Frepp · Sepp
suppliers.note: The incumbent in 2% CHG / 70% alcohol applicators, and the origin of the whole chlorhexidine thread — a sterility recall plus a separate production-line supply issue. See live issues.

suppliers.brands: Prevantics
suppliers.note: The nearest like-for-like to ChloraPrep on the catalogue: DEC85019 swabstick, DEC85017 26ml and DEC85034 10.5ml applicators. Now capped by Protect Demand Management itself — see live issues.

suppliers.brands: Clinell · HEXI
suppliers.note: GAMA's own site describes HEXI as "2% CHG in 70% IPA solutions for intravenous care" — the same formulation as ChloraPrep, from a supplier not caught by either notice.

suppliers.brands: 2% Chlorhexidine 70% Isopropanol
suppliers.note: Bottled solutions DEC85071 (tinted) and DEC85072 (clear). Also the cannulation packs whose 13 codes are suspended because ChloraPrep is a component — see live issues.

suppliers.brands: CoClens
suppliers.note: The widest bottled chlorhexidine range on the catalogue: DEC85002 500ml clear, DEC85023 200ml, DEC85027 200ml red-staining ready-to-apply, plus 0.5% sprays. A bottle is a different infection-control conversation from a single-use applicator.

suppliers.brands: Hibi range
suppliers.note: Hibiwash 500ml (4% chlorhexidine gluconate) carries its own Class 2 medicines recall — filed under Matched to a tracked product, not here.

suppliers.brands: octenisan
suppliers.note: Octenidine rather than chlorhexidine, so unaffected by the CHG supply pressure — worth knowing when a trust is rationed.

suppliers.brands: Vernacare
suppliers.note: Awarded on the framework; patient cleansing and hygiene rather than pre-operative antisepsis.

route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Examination Gloves (4 lots, 19 suppliers). Lot 1 is 6N Nitrile, Lot 2 Specialised, Lot 3 Vinyl, Lot 4 Latex
NHS Supply Chain — Clinical and Sharps Waste Management (7 lots, 14 suppliers)
route.note: Re-checked against the contract launch brief on 21/08/2026: the extension has been taken. The brief now states a 48-month term ending 23/10/2027, including a 12-month extension, and the page was last modified 14/08/2026. The earlier 31/10/2026 end date is superseded. Reference 2022/S 000-028722, 14 suppliers, seven lots.

route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Polymer Aprons (8 suppliers), reference 2023/S 000-014652, Medical and Surgical Consumables
route.note: Aprons have their own stocked framework, separate from the wider PPE route.

route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Polymer Products (5 suppliers), reference 2022/S 171-486016, Medical and Surgical Consumables
route.note: Bags, sheeting and polymer consumables. Ends within a year — check for a successor before quoting it.

route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Reusable Clinical and Sharps Waste Management Service (3 suppliers), reference 2025/S 000-078535, Medical and Surgical Consumables
route.note: A SERVICE framework, not a product one: the award is for managing the waste stream, so the buyer and the sales conversation are both different from a consumables pitch.

infection.routeNote: Two routes. Examination Gloves is four lots (6N nitrile, specialised, vinyl, latex) — surgical gloves sit on their own framework and hand hygiene on another again, so a glove conversation and a hand-hygiene conversation are different buying routes even with the same infection prevention lead. Clinical and Sharps Waste Management is seven lots covering sharps and clinical waste containers, swab holders, sharps pads, needle counters and needle/blade removers — and it now runs to 23/10/2027 following a 12-month extension confirmed on the launch brief (re-checked 21/08/2026). route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Laboratory Diagnostics, Point of Care Testing and Pathology Managed Services (7 usable lots, 122 suppliers, 19 of them new). Lot 5 is Laboratory Equipment and Consumables

pathology.routeNote: Seven lots in use: managed services, blood and cellular sciences, genomics, point of care testing, laboratory equipment and consumables, digital pathology and imaging, and one-stop. 122 awarded suppliers, the second largest framework the Hub tracks. Much of pathology is bought as a managed service on long contracts, so a consumable conversation and an analyser conversation are very different sales. The set below is the histology and consumables end, not all 122. More companies from the Hub's verified supplier index are listed below without catalogue-level product detail yet (marked as such in their row) — added 02/09/2026 from the index the Hub already held, not fresh research.

route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Advanced Wound Care (18 lots, 56 suppliers, 13 of them new)
NHS Supply Chain — General Wound Care (Stocked, eDirect, 28 suppliers)
route.note: Basic dressings, bandages, tapes, plasters and first aid — the separate framework the Advanced Wound Care routeNote already pointed at. Crest Medical Ltd is named on this award list. Added 19/08/2026 after 872 of Crest Medical's crawled divisions (workplace, motorist and travel first aid kits, plasters, crepe and triangular bandages, eye pads, ambulance dressings, saline wound-cleansing spray) turned up with nowhere to go in the four Advanced Wound Care types.

wound.routeNote: Eighteen lots covering hydrogels, gelling fibres and alginates, wound contact layers, super absorbents, foams, hydrocolloids, IV and film dressings, burns and scar management, irrigation, debridement, adhesive removers, skin protectants, compression bandages and adhesive tapes. wound.dacsNote: These are NOT on the framework above and do not compete for it. A Dispensing Appliance Contractor (DAC) is an NHS-registered organisation authorised to dispense against an FP10/GP10 prescription and be reimbursed at the Drug Tariff price — patients choose one directly or on a clinician's recommendation, and the DAC then supplies whichever brand is prescribed, from any manufacturer. Verified from each DAC's own website on 12/08/2026, not from the Drug Tariff or an NHS Supply Chain framework — DAC registration itself is not published on a single public list.

route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Endoscopy, Endourology and Oncology Ablation Consumables and Associated Products (3 lots, 58 suppliers, 17 of them new)

gastro.routeNote: The same framework the Endoscopy speciality uses, viewed from the GI end: Lot 1 is Endoscopy, Lot 2 Endourology, Lot 3 Oncology Ablation. Endoscopy on this tool is scope-led; this set is the therapeutic GI consumable — what goes down the channel to stop a bleed, take a polyp or hold a stricture open. NHS Supply Chain publishes only a framework-wide supplier list, with no breakdown of who is awarded on which lot, so lot membership is not asserted for any supplier here. Scopes themselves and the washer-disinfectors that reprocess them are bought on separate frameworks. route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Endoscopy, Endourology and Oncology Ablation Consumables and Associated Products (Lot 2 is Endourology; 58 suppliers across 3 lots)
NHS Supply Chain — Lithotripsy and Associated Options and Related Services (fixed and non-fixed lithotripter systems, 3 suppliers)

endourology.routeNote: Two routes, and they are opposite ends of the same patient pathway. The consumables — stents, baskets, guidewires, access sheaths, laser fibres — sit in Lot 2 of the endoscopy framework alongside 57 other suppliers. The lithotripters themselves sit on their own framework with just THREE awarded suppliers, fixed and non-fixed systems, and it runs to 2028. A three-supplier capital framework is the most concentrated field in this tool; a rep working stone disease needs to know both, because the consumable spend follows whichever machine the trust already owns. route.name: NHS Commercial Solutions — Pharmacy frameworks (the services and equipment around medicines, not the medicines themselves)
route.noExpiry: A rolling programme of separate framework agreements, each re-tendered on its own cycle, so there is no single expiry date to count down to. Check the individual framework with the purchasing point or the MPSC catalogue.

pharma.routeNote: ⚠ MEDICINES DO NOT GO THROUGH NHS SUPPLY CHAIN. Everything else in this tool is bought on an NHS Supply Chain framework with a public catalogue and a published award list. Medicines are not. They are bought on NHS England MPSC frameworks — the team formerly called the Commercial Medicines Unit — which "establishes the commercial arrangements to enable the purchasing of medicines prescribed in NHS hospitals in England". The named framework categories are: generic medicines used in hospital; generic medicines used in primary care; clozapine; sevoflurane; tranche medicines; national branded category; intravenous fluids; influenza vaccine; aseptically prepared chemotherapy and monoclonal antibodies for cancer; low molecular weight heparins and fondaparinux; hereditary angioedema; blood disorders including haemophilia A and B; and patent-expiring medicines. ·· TWO THINGS THAT CHANGE HOW YOU SELL. First, PRICES ARE CONFIDENTIAL: only "authorised NHS pharmacy staff" can see them, via the MPSC web catalogue. There is no public price list to work from and no published award list, which is why there is no comparison table below. Second, and the one most people get wrong: INDEPENDENT SECTOR PROVIDERS ARE EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE for MPSC framework prices — NHS England's published position lists them as out of scope "irrespective of the volume of NHS patients supported", alongside general primary care providers and community pharmacies. So a private hospital cannot buy at these prices even when treating NHS patients; it buys through wholesalers and its own group arrangements. A small number of private patients treated inside NHS organisations are the narrow exception, and even then the purchasing point "must request approval to purchase at MPSC framework prices from the relevant framework holder in advance". ·· The services AROUND medicines — homecare, pharmaceutical wholesale, aseptic isolators and cleanroom consumables, radiopharmaceuticals, contrast media, pharmacy robots and specialist couriers — are a different route again, run by NHS collaborative procurement organisations. That is often the more accessible way in for a supplier who is not a medicines manufacturer. ·· READING THE RECALL CLASSES, in the MHRA's own words from its Guide to Defective Medicinal Products, because the class tells you how hard to push and most people guess. A National Patient Safety Alert, equivalent to the old Class 1, means "the defect presents a risk of death or disability". Class 2 means "the defect may cause mistreatment or harm to the patient, but it is not life-threatening or serious". Class 3 means "the defect is unlikely to cause harm to the patient, and the recall is carried out for other reasons, such as non-compliance with the marketing authorisation or specification". Class 4 is a Notification, not a recall — a "Caution in Use" notice "where there is no threat to patients or no serious defect likely to impair product use or efficacy", generally minor defects in packaging or printed materials. ·· THE NON-OBVIOUS ONE, and the reason to read Class 4s rather than skip them: the MHRA also issues them "where a defect has been identified but due to supply concerns product cannot be recalled". A Class 4 can therefore be a SUPPLY signal wearing a labelling headline — the product is defective enough to warn about and too scarce to pull. ·· Note too that most recalls are Class 2 or 3 and stop at pharmacy or wholesaler level: the MHRA's own guidance says patient-level recalls are rarely required at that risk level because "recalls may present a greater risk to the patient than continuing treatment". So a Class 2 landing in a hospital pharmacy is a stock and substitution problem, not a ward-level emergency.

pharma.noSuppliers: There is no public competitor set for medicines, so none is shown. NHS England's MPSC frameworks publish no award list, and their prices are confidential to authorised NHS pharmacy staff — unlike every NHS Supply Chain framework in this tool, whose catalogue and awarded suppliers are open. route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Pressure Area Care and Patient Handling (53 suppliers), reference 2025/S 000-086469, Rehabilitation and Community

ostomy.label: Ostomy and stoma care

route.name: NHSBSA Drug Tariff Part IXC — Stoma Appliances and Associated Products. Not an NHS Supply Chain framework: stoma appliances are dispensed on prescription and reimbursed at the Part IX price. 8,223 listings from 68 suppliers in the August 2026 edition
route.dates: Reissued monthly — figures below are the August 2026 edition
route.noExpiry: Part IX has no start or end date. It is reissued every month and prices can change with each edition, so a price quoted from it is only good for that month.

ostomy.routeNote: THIS IS A DIFFERENT ROUTE TO MARKET FROM THE REST OF THIS TAB, and selling it as if it were NHS Supply Chain will lose the account. There is no framework to win, no tender and no award: a product gets a Part IX listing, a patient is prescribed it, and the dispenser is reimbursed at the Tariff price. The decision sits with the stoma care nurse specialist and the patient, and the volume flows through dispensing appliance contractors, not a trust's procurement team. Prices below are the Drug Tariff reimbursement price in the August 2026 edition and change monthly. 68 suppliers hold Part IXC listings; the ten below are the largest by listing count, together covering 5,478 of the 8,223 listings. More companies from the Hub's verified supplier index are listed below without catalogue-level product detail yet (marked as such in their row) — added 02/09/2026 from the index the Hub already held, not fresh research.

A Dispensing Appliance Contractor (DAC) is an NHS-registered organisation authorised to dispense against an FP10/GP10 prescription and be reimbursed at the Drug Tariff price — patients choose one directly or on a clinician's recommendation, and the DAC then supplies whichever brand is prescribed, from any manufacturer. route.name: NHSBSA Drug Tariff Part IX — sensors, lancets and pen needles in Part IXA, blood glucose and ketone test strips in Part IXR. This is how the volume is bought: on prescription, reimbursed at the Tariff price

route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Insulin Pumps, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Products Contributing to the Delivery of Hybrid Closed Loop Pathways and Associated Products (12 suppliers), reference 2025/S 000-4043, supply route Direct

diabetes.routeNote: TWO ROUTES, AND THEY ARE NOT ALTERNATIVES. The NHS Supply Chain framework above is real and names 12 suppliers — Abbott, Advanced Therapeutics, Air Liquide Healthcare, Dexcom, Glooko, GlucoRX Technologies, Insulet, Medtronic, Medtrum, Novo Nordisk, Urathon and Ypsomed — but it is the access route for pumps and hybrid closed loop, not how the consumable volume transacts. Sensors, strips, lancets and pen needles are prescribed and reimbursed through Part IX. The Hub's own catalogue check has already recorded FreeStyle Libre 2 Plus and 3 Plus as “Drug Tariff Part IX prescription” and MiniMed 780G with Guardian CGM as “insulin pump/CGM via prescription” — none of them is an NHS Supply Chain catalogue line, so none has an NPC code to quote. The table below is the Part IX competitor set. Insulet, Medtronic, Ypsomed, Medtrum, Glooko, Air Liquide, Advanced Therapeutics and Urathon hold no Part IX listing of their own and so do not appear in it; they are on the framework, which is a different question from being on the Tariff. THE PRICES ARE DIRECTLY COMPARABLE and rarely are: every row in the `cgm` column is a sensor reimbursed at a published monthly price, so this is one of the few genuinely like-for-like price comparisons on this tab. It changes every month — re-read the current edition before quoting it. More companies from the Hub's verified supplier index are listed below without catalogue-level product detail yet (marked as such in their row) — added 02/09/2026 from the index the Hub already held, not fresh research.

neuro.label: Neurosurgery and neuromodulation

route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Neuromodulation Devices and Associated Products (23 suppliers), reference 2023/S 000-034841, Medical Technology

neuro.routeNote: eDirect, so the trust orders against the framework but the device is delivered and supported by the manufacturer — the rep is in the room for the implant, not just the tender. 23 suppliers are named on the brief; the seven below are those whose implants this repo can evidence line by line in the catalogue. Every code below is an HCTED line: high-cost tariff-excluded, reimbursed to the trust separately from the procedure, which is why price alone rarely decides it. More companies from the Hub's verified supplier index are listed below without catalogue-level product detail yet (marked as such in their row) — added 02/09/2026 from the index the Hub already held, not fresh research.

types.shockwave: Non-invasive neuromodulation & extracorporeal shockwave therapy — distinct from implantable devices (scs/dbs/sns/pns)

suppliers.brands: Proclaim Elite · Proclaim DRG · Proclaim 5 · Proclaim 7
suppliers.note: 9 catalogue lines, all spinal cord stimulation. Proclaim 5 (FNV002) and Proclaim 7 (FNV003) implantable pulse generators; Proclaim DRG (FMA787) is the non-rechargeable dorsal root ganglion device — the only DRG line here, so on that indication it has no listed competitor.

suppliers.brands: Vercise · Spectra WaveWriter · Axonics
suppliers.note: The widest span of the seven: Vercise deep brain stimulation (FCP065 charger, FCP87449 patient programmer), Spectra WaveWriter spinal cord (FCP183), and Axonics sacral nerve (FCP86555). Competes with Medtronic on all three.

suppliers.brands: Percept · Intellis · InterStim X
suppliers.note: Percept deep brain (FCP85120), Intellis spinal cord (FCP85830), InterStim X sacral nerve (FMA85002). Head-to-head with Boston Scientific across all three modalities.

suppliers.brands: Senza · Senza II
suppliers.note: Spinal cord stimulation only — Senza rechargeable IPG (FMA721) and Senza II (FMA1010). A single-modality specialist against three full-range majors.

suppliers.brands: EASEE
suppliers.note: The full EASEE system on four lines: power unit (FMA85013), lead (FCP85851), physician programmer (FCP85850) and patient accessories (FCP85849). A single-product entrant.

suppliers.brands: ReActiv8
suppliers.note: ReActiv8 (FMA1591) with its self-anchoring electrodes (FCP86855), stimulating the dorsal ramus medial branch for mechanical low back pain — a different target from the spinal cord devices above, so not a like-for-like substitute.

suppliers.brands: Inspire
suppliers.note: Peripheral nerve stimulation for obstructive sleep apnoea (FCP85858). One line, one indication, and no listed competitor on this framework.

types.materials: Orthotic fabrication materials and componentry (EVA and CAD/CAM stock, coverings, alloy bar and tubing, fixings, pads)

suppliers.brands: Footmedics · DiabetiX · KinetiX · Prolevo FootSafe
suppliers.note: 29 relevant catalogue lines, the most of any supplier here and almost all podiatry. DiabetiX full-length functional insole for the diabetic foot (ERU86229), KinetiX (ERU85632), Footmedics gel cushions (ERP1582), Prolevo FootSafe prevention boot (GRA5228).

suppliers.note: 20 lines, entirely graduated compression hosiery across both classes — mediven Plus Class 1 (EGB86491, EGD9781) and Elegance Class 1 and 2 (EGD10343, EGD9823). The compression specialist rather than a general orthotics supplier.

suppliers.brands: MD Orthopaedics · Dorsi Ramp · ADM Modular Brace System

suppliers.brands: Turbomed

suppliers.brands: Malleo Dynastab · Malleo Dynastab Vario · Malleo Dynastab Boa

digital.routeNote: Both frameworks are real and both are live; between them they name 74 suppliers. What does not exist is a product comparison, and inventing one here would be the tool lying to a rep. `tec` and `aac` types added 25/08/2026 on Lou's decision for Possum Ltd's telecare/AAC/environmental-control range, found in the crawl with nowhere to go. digital.noSuppliers: NO CATALOGUE-VERIFIED COMPETITOR SET IS POSSIBLE FOR SOFTWARE, and that is a fact about how it is bought rather than a gap in this repo. Every other table on this tab is built from NHS Supply Chain catalogue lines with NPC codes; software and managed services are bought Direct, produce no catalogue line, and have no comparable unit — a per-seat licence, a per-study fee and a capital deployment are not the same thing and cannot sit in one price column. The two frameworks above ARE the route to market and both name their suppliers on the brief, so open them. What a rep needs here is the business case and the information-governance answer, not a features grid: procurement is not the decision-maker for clinical software, the CCIO and the trust's digital board usually are.

dermatology.label: Dermatology
dermatology.routeNote: No NHS Supply Chain framework covers dermatology as a category. This is not an omission in the capture: 125 contract launch briefs were read and none of them is dermatology.
dermatology.noSuppliers: DERMATOLOGY HAS NO SINGLE ROUTE TO MARKET, WHICH IS WHY THERE IS NO TABLE HERE. Its three product groups are each bought somewhere else entirely. Emollients and topical preparations are prescribed and reimbursed through the NHSBSA Drug Tariff, not NHS Supply Chain. Teledermatology and AI lesion-triage platforms are clinical software bought Direct on the Digital Diagnostic Solutions framework — see Digital health and clinical software. Phototherapy units are capital equipment, usually a trust-level business case. speciality-map.json has recorded the missing NHSSC framework entry for dermatology as PENDING since 20/07/2026 rather than guessing a URL, and that remains the right answer. A rep selling into dermatology should start from which of those three routes their product travels, because the buyer is different in each.

types.energy: Energy-based dermatology and aesthetic devices (laser, shockwave and phototherapy platforms)

surgical.routeNote: Reusable stainless-steel hand instruments. NHS Supply Chain's Surgical Instruments framework (reference 2020/S 170-412524, supply route Direct, Stocked and eDirect) names 50 awarded suppliers. The table below shows the 8 that pass all three evidence tests: named on the award list, own website proved against the company registration number published on that site, and an instrument range actually read from their own catalogue — so the families listed are what each supplier demonstrably sells, not what it might sell. The other 42 are named on the framework but not listed here: 29 have no verified website on record and 13 have a verified website but no instrument range read from it, and neither is a reason to send a rep to a page chosen on a guess. Reconcile against the framework total of 50; this table grows as those are proved. Single-use instrument ranges are deliberately excluded — they are theatre consumables and sit under Theatres, so a reusable instrument is never compared against a sterile single-use equivalent.
